title: Per-model usage attribution with a Tools/summaries bucket, plus a priced cache-miss total
one_line: Split the session's flat token/cost total into one row per model that actually served tokens plus one literal "Tools/summaries" row, then add a priced total for the prompt-cache misses the agent caused.
user_visible_effect: `/info` gains an "Attribution" section listing each model that actually burned tokens, its token counts and dollar cost, sorted by cost descending, plus a "Tools/summaries" row for compaction/branch-summary/subagent calls the agent made on your behalf, and a "Cache misses" line reporting how many tokens were re-paid at cache-read price and what that cost. `/usage` (ACP text mode) gains the same per-model block above its existing flat totals. A user who switched models mid-session can finally see which model is actually spending the money, and can see the agent's own summarization cost separated from the model they chose.
risk: Double counting. The three usage sources (assistant message, `task` tool result, `model_usage` entry) must each land in exactly ONE bucket, and a `model_usage` entry must never also be credited to a model row. The plan is explicit that this is the single easiest way to get the item wrong, and it is why the two layers are one work item: layer two's cache-miss cost has nowhere correct to land without layer one's bucketing. The second risk is picking the wrong identity field -- the plan says `responseModel`, which does not exist on `AssistantMessage` in this repo (see plan_corrections); using `message.model` alone silently mis-attributes every provider-alias turn.
gate: Two commands, both must be green. (1) `bun run check:ts` from the repo root -- oxlint + oxfmt + `tsgo --noEmit` across every package; it catches the type errors that a blocked `bun test` cannot. (2) Once the native addon is built (`bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`), `bun test packages/coding-agent/test/usage-breakdown.test.ts packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/usage-statistics.test.ts` -- the new file plus the pre-existing file whose totals it refactors, so a regression in the flat totals is caught by the suite that already pins them. Additionally, `/info` must render a non-empty Attribution section for a session that used two models plus a compaction; run it in the TUI and confirm the `Tools/summaries` row is present and that the per-row costs sum to the unchanged `Cost: Total` line already on screen. WHY THE GATE CAN FAIL: The gate goes red if the bucketing is wrong in the way that matters: if a `model_usage` entry (compaction / auto-thinking / judgment / subagent `task` result) is also added to a model row, the new test's equality assertion (`sum of per-row costs === the single flat total`, and `Tools/summaries` row cost > 0 with no model row carrying it) fails, and the pre-existing `usage-statistics.test.ts` totals also drift. If `upstreamModel` fallback is omitted, the provider-alias test fails. If the noise floor is not applied, the sub-1024-token miss test asserts a non-zero cost and fails. If the sticky rule is not implemented, the read-only-provider test and the no-caching-provider test produce the same result and the discriminating test fails. `bun run check:ts` independently goes red on any type error, and I confirmed it is currently green at HEAD, so it is a real signal and not a pre-existing red.
open_questions: Where exactly should the per-model rows render in `/info` -- inside the existing `Cost` block (command-controller.ts:415-431) or as a new `Attribution` section immediately after it? Recommend a new section, because the existing `Cost` block also carries Credits and Premium Requests which have no per-model meaning; folding rows into it would imply those are attributed too.

Should `/usage` (the ACP text path, `buildUsageReportText`) gain the per-model block when it has provider-reported limits? The provider-reported branch returns early (usage-report.ts:175-186) and never reaches the local tallies. Recommend adding the block only to the local-tallies fallback branch, and noting in a comment that the provider-reported branch has no per-model data by construction.

Is the `Tools/summaries` bucket name a literal that ships, or should it be a shared exported constant? Recommend exporting `TOOLS_SUMMARIES_BUCKET` from the new module and using it in both the aggregator and the renderer, so a later rename is one edit -- but the plan specifies the literal string, so confirm the name is final before other work items (W17) hard-code it in a bug-report template.

bun --cwd=packages/natives run build   # unblocks bun test; currently the only blocker

bun test packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/usage-statistics.test.ts
test_contract: The consumer is a human asking "which model is actually costing me money, and what did the agent spend summarizing my own context?" If this regresses, the user sees one blended total and cannot tell that a background compaction burned half the session, or that a mid-session model switch moved the bill to a model they stopped using ten turns ago. Concretely the tests defend four observable contracts: (1) the per-model rows plus the `Tools/summaries` row sum EXACTLY to the pre-existing flat total -- this is the double-count guard and the reason the pre-existing `usage-statistics.test.ts` must be re-run alongside; (2) a `model_usage` entry produced by compaction lands in the `Tools/summaries` bucket and in NO model row; (3) an assistant message whose `upstreamModel` differs from `model` is attributed to the served model, not the requested one; (4) a cache miss below the noise floor reports zero missed tokens and zero missed cost. Consumer-visible regression: rows that double-count would make the Attribution section sum to more than the `Cost: Total` the user is already looking at -- an arithmetic impossibility the UI makes obvious, which is why contract (1) is written as an equality against the untouched flat total rather than as a snapshot.

steps.instruction: Confirm the baseline before touching anything: run `bun run check:ts` from the repo root and confirm it is green. I verified this on 2026-09-27 at HEAD ecd516f and it passed. NOTE the working tree is shared with other milestone-1 workers writing to the same branch -- I observed a transient red on packages/coding-agent/test/collab/w3-probe.test.ts (a file that did not exist on disk when I re-checked seconds later). If check:ts is red, first confirm the offending file is not one you created before assuming your change broke it.

Create packages/coding-agent/src/session/usage-breakdown.ts. Export the three constants (TOOLS_SUMMARIES_BUCKET, NOISE_FLOOR_TOKENS, CACHE_ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW_MS) and the three types (UsageBucket, CacheMissCost, UsageBreakdown), then a single pure exported function `buildUsageBreakdown(input)`. Keep it pure and read-only: no session-manager calls, no registry calls, no Date.now() inside -- the caller passes `nowMs`. Dependency injection for the price lookup (`cacheReadRatePerMillion`) so the function is testable without a ModelRegistry.

Implement layer one, the per-model buckets, by copying the walk that getSessionStats() already performs -- this is the important move, because that function at session-stats.ts:114-205 is ALREADY doing the three-source walk; W9 splits its single flat accumulator into per-key buckets rather than inventing a new traversal. Three sources, each landing in exactly one bucket: (a) assistant messages, keyed `${msg.provider}/${msg.upstreamModel ?? msg.model}`; (b) tool results where `message.toolName === "task"`, reading usage out of `message.details` exactly as `taskToolUsage` does at session-stats.ts:422-426 -- these go to the Tools/summaries bucket because a `task` tool result is a subagent the agent spawned, not the user's model; (c) `model_usage` entries from the branch, selected by `activeModelUsageEntries(branch)` (session-stats.ts:63-76) -- these also go to Tools/summaries. Increment `turns` only for source (a). Accumulate input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost using the same fields `addUsage` reads at session-stats.ts:134-151 so the two aggregators cannot drift apart.

Add the final filter-and-sort the plan specifies, reproducing pi's `.filter(entry => entry.cost > 0 || entry.tokens > 0).sort((a, b) => b.cost - a.cost)`: drop any bucket whose cost and totalTokens are both zero, then sort by cost descending. Ties broken by key ascending for a stable render. Keep the Tools/summaries row in this same list -- it is a peer row, not a footer.

Implement layer two, the priced cache-miss total, in the same function. Walk the assistant messages in order; for each one that is NOT already explained (`transcript.cacheMissExplainedAt[i] !== true`, the array built at session-context.ts:364-378), compute idleMs as the gap from the previous assistant message's `completedAt ?? timestamp` to this message's `timestamp`. A miss is counted only when ALL of: cacheRead === 0 this turn, reprocessedTokens (cacheWrite + input) > 0, reprocessedTokens >= NOISE_FLOOR_TOKENS, and idleMs >= CACHE_ATTRIBUTION_WINDOW_MS or a model change preceded it. `missedTokens += reprocessedTokens`. `missedCost += reprocessedTokens / 1_000_000 * cacheReadRatePerMillion(provider, servedId)` -- the division is required because Model.cost.cacheRead is a PER-MILLION rate (packages/catalog/src/types.ts:1116-1122 'Per-million-token rates for one model pricing tier'), while Usage.cost.* is already dollars. When the rate lookup returns undefined, add tokens but not cost.

Implement the STICKY model-change signal -- this is the subtle branch the plan flags and the one most likely to be done wrong. Do not read the boolean straight off trackMessageCacheState. Instead: set `providerReportsCaching = true` on the bucket as soon as ANY turn in the session shows `cacheRead > 0 || cacheWrite > 0`; only while it is still false does a model change explain a miss. This is what makes a read-only-cache provider (OpenAI: reports cacheRead, never cacheWrite) distinguishable from a provider that reports no caching at all -- the first will have flipped the flag by the time its cold turn arrives, the second never will, so the second keeps getting the model-change explanation. Record `modelChanged` per contributing miss, and OR them into the total.

Wire the aggregator into the session stats path. Add `usageBreakdown` to the `SessionStats` interface (optional, so the many existing `getSessionStats()` callers and test fixtures that build a partial SessionStats keep type-checking -- there are literal-object fixtures at packages/coding-agent/src/cli/gallery-fixtures/preview-session.ts:43 and status-line.ts:40 that would otherwise break). Compute it inside SessionStatsTracker after the existing walk, reusing the already-collected routedModels/branch data so the Attribution block and the existing flat totals are provably derived from the same pass.

Render the Attribution section in the session info view. Insert it in handleSessionCommand() immediately after the existing Cost block (which ends at command-controller.ts:431) so per-model spend sits next to the total it decomposes. One line per row: key, totalTokens, and cost to 4 decimals -- matching the existing `stats.cost.toFixed(4)` at command-controller.ts:420 so the column is visually consistent. Then a `Cache misses:` line with `missedTokens` and `missedCost.toFixed(4)`, omitted entirely when missedTokens is 0. Sanitize the key with replaceTabs + sanitizeText before interpolating -- the existing routedModels render at command-controller.ts:384 does exactly this, follow it. Skip the whole section when there are no rows.

Add the per-model block to the ACP `/usage` text path, in the local-tallies fallback branch only (after the early return at usage-report.ts:186, alongside the existing `Cost: $...` line). This branch is a plain-text TUI-sanitized string, not a theme-rendered overlay, so use plain lines and run model keys through sanitizeText. Leave the provider-reported branch untouched and add a one-line comment saying why (it has no per-model data by construction). Note that buildUsageReportText is confirmed to be the ONLY export of usage-report.ts, so this file needs no new export surface.

Write packages/coding-agent/test/usage-breakdown.test.ts. Use `SessionManager.inMemory()` + `appendMessage` / `appendModelUsage` / `buildSessionContext()` as the fixture seam -- that is exactly the pattern in the existing packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/usage-statistics.test.ts, and it gives a real branch and a real cacheMissExplainedAt without mocks. Cover: (1) two models plus one compaction -- assert the rows sum to the flat `getUsageStatistics().cost` AND that the compaction's usage is in the Tools/summaries row and in no model row; (2) provider alias -- an assistant message with `upstreamModel` differing from `model` attributes to the served id; (3) real idle-gap miss reports missedTokens > 0 with missedCost equal to `missedTokens / 1e6 * rate`, while a miss under the noise floor reports exactly 0 and 0; (4) the sticky discrimination -- a provider that reported a warm cacheRead on an earlier turn and then goes cold is NOT attributed to a model change, while a provider whose turns report neither cacheRead nor cacheWrite at all still is. Four distinct branches, no duplicated rows, every assertion naming a consumer-visible outcome. Do NOT assert on prompt/label wording.

Re-run packages/coding-agent/test/session-manager/usage-statistics.test.ts. It pins the flat totals your step-7 refactor touches; if it drifts, layer one is double counting. Note this file cannot run until the native addon is built -- `bun --cwd=packages/natives run build`. Until then `bun run check:ts` is your only executable signal.

Add a one-line entry under `## [Unreleased]` / `### Added` in packages/coding-agent/CHANGELOG.md, user-facing, no implementation detail: "`/info` now breaks down token cost by the model that actually served each turn, separates the agent's own summarization into a Tools/summaries row, and reports the dollar cost of prompt-cache misses." Per AGENTS.md this is an internal change with no issue link, so plain wording.

plan_corrections.claim: Bucket 'ALL tool results with usage' AND 'branch_summary/compaction entries with usage' into the literal "Tools/summaries" key.
plan_corrections.verdict: WRONG SHAPES -- the real entry points are different
plan_corrections.correction: Two of the three named shapes do not exist as described. (a) `ToolResultMessage` (packages/ai/src/types.ts:1178-1198) has NO `usage` field -- the only usage a tool result can carry is nested inside `details`, and only the `task` tool result's details do: `taskToolUsage(details)` at session-stats.ts:422-426 reads `Reflect.get(details, 'usage')` and guards it with `isUsage` (428-438). The real predicate is `message.toolName === "task"` (session-stats.ts:155-158), not 'any tool result with usage'. (b) `CompactionEntry` (session-entries.ts:121+) has NO `usage` field -- it carries `summary, shortSummary, firstKeptEntryId, tokensBefore, tokensAfter, method, details, preserveData, fromExtension`. Compaction/branch-summary usage is recorded out-of-band as a separate `ModelUsageEntry` with `type: "model_usage"` (session-entries.ts:80-91, carrying `purpose, role, api, provider, model, usage, stopReason`), written by `SessionManager.appendModelUsage()` at session-manager.ts:2820-2839. The third source is therefore `activeModelUsageEntries(branch)` at session-stats.ts:63-76. Net effect on the work: the bucket's membership is right in spirit (agent-initiated calls, not the user's model) but the three selectors must be rewritten. Observed `purpose` values: `"auto-thinking"` (model-controls.ts:634-637) and free-form judgment purposes (judgment/index.ts:78-85).

The nearest existing analogue is `MIN_CACHE_FOOTPRINT = 2048` at packages/tui/src/chat/cache-invalidation-marker.ts:12, which serves the same purpose (filter out sub-footprint cache collapses) but is deliberately gated BEHIND a prior warm read (`prev.cacheRead < MIN_CACHE_FOOTPRINT` at :55). `CACHE_TTL_MS` also does not exist; the 5-minute value is `ANTHROPIC_CACHE_TTL_MS = 5 * 60_000` at packages/ai/src/stream.ts:1209. Recommend 2048 for internal consistency, and note that `detectCacheInvalidation` already encodes the sharper provider-discrimination rule the plan's 'sticky' note is reaching for: it requires `current.cacheWrite > 0` (:61) precisely because implicit-cache providers report cacheWrite 0 (doc comment at :29-44). Read that function before writing layer two -- it is the best existing statement of the semantics and reusing its reasoning avoids a second, subtly different rule.
